Claude Sonnet 5.5 Cache Read Price Cut · AI Signal

 By Álvaro Lucero Rufino October 13, 2026 pricing anthropic prompt-caching 

# Claude Sonnet 5.5 Cache Reads Fall to $0.10: The Bill Math

 Source Anthropic platform release notes (October 7, 2026) and pricing page, read on October 13, 2026 ↗ 

On October 7, 2026 Anthropic halved one price of Claude Sonnet 5.5: reading a prompt from the cache now costs $0.10 per million tokens instead of $0.20. Nothing else moved. This post checks the change against Anthropic’s own pages, read again on October 13, 2026, puts it next to the cache prices of the models around it, and works out what it does to the monthly bill of one cached workload at three hit rates. The release notes give no reason for the change, and this post does not guess one.

## What Anthropic changed, in its own words

The platform release notes entry for October 7, 2026 reads: “We’ve lowered the price of prompt cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 from $0.20 USD to $0.10 USD per million tokens: 0.05x the base input price instead of 0.1x. Cache writes and all other prices are unchanged.”

Anthropic’s pricing page, read on October 13, 2026, prints the row as `Claude Sonnet 5.5 | The best combination of speed and intelligence | $2 / MTok | $10 / MTok | $2.50 / MTok | $4 / MTok | $0.10 / MTok` (input, output, 5-minute cache write, 1-hour cache write, cache read). Its caching table now names the model in the exception: “Cache read (hit) | 0.1x base input price (0.025x on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1; 0.05x on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5)”. This site recorded the change on its price-changes page as a decrease by the provider, effective October 7, 2026, after reading the new figure on October 11. All five figures on the page match the dataset row, verified on October 12.

| Claude Sonnet 5.5, per 1M tokens | Until October 6, 2026 | From October 7, 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input | $2.00 | $2.00 |
| Output | $10.00 | $10.00 |
| Cache write, 5 minutes | $2.50 | $2.50 |
| Cache write, 1 hour | $4.00 | $4.00 |
| Cache read | $0.20 | $0.10 |

## Next to the other Claude models

The models a Sonnet 5.5 user is most likely to weigh it against, with the prices on Anthropic’s page on October 13, 2026:

| Model | Status in this dataset | Input | Cache read | Cache read as share of input |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | current | $0.10 | $0.01 | 0.1x |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | current | $2.00 | $0.10 | 0.05x |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | current | $4.00 | $0.20 | 0.05x |
| Claude Sonnet 4.6 | current | $3.00 | $0.30 | 0.1x |
| Claude Sonnet 4.5 | deprecated, retires November 30, 2026 | $3.00 | $0.30 | 0.1x |

Haiku 5.5’s figures are its list for prompts up to 100,000 tokens; above that line every one of its prices is five times higher, as our post on its threshold works through. Claude Sonnet 5, which Anthropic now lists under “Additional models”, still prints $0.20 for cache reads with the same $2, $10, $2.50 and $4 as Sonnet 5.5, so since October 7 the two differ on that one line only.

Sonnet 5.5 came out after our cache price survey of September 16, which found a cache hit at 10% of the input price to be the norm. It launched at that norm, $0.20 on $2, and since October 7 sits below it, with Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1.

## What the cache-write rule adds

A cache read is only half of the arithmetic. The pricing page’s caching table lists “5-minute cache write | 1.25x base input price | Cache valid for 5 minutes” and “1-hour cache write | 2x base input price | Cache valid for 1 hour”, and explains when each is charged: “Cache write tokens are charged when content is first stored. Cache read tokens are charged when a subsequent request retrieves the cached content.” The October 7 change touched neither write price, so on Sonnet 5.5 a 5-minute write still costs $2.50 per million tokens, 25 times the new read price.

# Anthropic Halves Sonnet 5.5 Cache-Read Price to $0.10 per Million Tokens

Editorial Team • October 7, 2026•📖 6 min read

Anthropic has halved Claude Sonnet 5.5’s cache-read price, matching OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol within its standard prompt tier. The company estimates around 20% savings on most agentic tasks, but the benefit depends on cached reuse and other workload charges.

- Claude Sonnet 5.5 cache reads now cost $0.10 per million tokens, down from $0.20; other token rates are unchanged.
- Anthropic’s estimated 20% saving on most agentic tasks depends on the share of spending devoted to cached input.
- The rate matches OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol for prompts within its standard pricing tier.

Anthropic, the developer and API provider of the Claude AI model family, cut Sonnet 5.5’s cache-read price on October 7. Sonnet is its model line for everyday production work, positioned between the smaller Haiku models and Opus for more demanding assignments. The reduction makes repeated use of documents, instructions and conversation history cheaper for applications already running Sonnet 5.5.

Anthropic’s company-reported Sonnet 5.5 rates distinguish cache reads from input, output and cache writes. MTok means one million tokens. Source: Claude Platform pricing.

## What changed on the bill

The October 7 entry in Anthropic’s release notes confirms the 50% reduction and explicitly leaves cache writes and all other prices unchanged. Tokens are the units of content the model processes and bills for.

Sonnet 5.5 launched on September 28 as the successor to Sonnet 5. At launch, Anthropic said its tests showed up to 30% lower cost per task because the newer model typically needed fewer tokens, despite unchanged token prices. This latest reduction changes an actual billing rate. The two savings claims have different bases and should not be added together.

Under Anthropic’s published pricing, Sonnet 5.5 now costs:

| Billing category | USD per million tokens |
| --- | --- |
| Uncached input | $2.00 |
| Output | $10.00 |

## Sources

- Anthropic
- Claude Platform release notes
- Claude Platform pricing
- VentureBeat
- Unite.AI
- Anthropic Sonnet 5.5 announcement
- OpenAI API changelog

| Five-minute cache write | $2.50 |
| --- | --- |

| One-hour cache write | $4.00 |
| --- | --- |

| Cache read | $0.10 |
| --- | --- |

Prompt caching lets an application reuse previously processed portions of a prompt across calls. Storing that content initially incurs a cache-write charge; retrieving it while the cache remains valid incurs the cheaper read charge. Anthropic offers five-minute and one-hour cache durations. The new read rate is 5% of Sonnet’s base input price, down from 10%.

That distinction matters for agents, which make successive model calls while working through a task. Reusing a long history can produce many cheap cache-read tokens, while newly supplied content and generated output still carry their usual charges.

Anthropic says in its announcement that the cut reduces Sonnet 5.5 costs on most agentic tasks by around 20%. The relevant measure is spending, not simply the proportion of tokens read from cache. Holding usage and every other charge constant, a 50% cut to one billing category reduces the total bill by 20% only if that category previously accounted for 40% of spending. The announcement provides no workload distribution that would let customers establish how closely they resemble Anthropic’s estimate.

## Cheaper reuse meets an existing rival

OpenAI, a competing AI model and API provider, released GPT-6.1 Sol for complex coding and professional work on September 29. Its release entry lists $2 input, $10 output, $2.50 cache writes and $0.10 cached input per million tokens for prompts with up to 272,000 input tokens. Those figures match Sonnet’s new standard rates when using Sonnet’s five-minute cache-write option.

Anthropic Slashes Claude Sonnet 5.5 Cache-Read Cost by 50% – Unite.AI

# Anthropic Slashes Claude Sonnet 5.5 Cache-Read Cost by 50%

 Published October 7, 2026 

By

 Jonas Reeve, Cognitive AI & AGI AI Research Agent 

Anthropic on October 7, 2026, lowered the price of cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 by 50%, from $0.20 to $0.10 per million tokens, effective immediately. The company also introduced a monthly Claude Platform API credit for Max and Team subscribers: $100 per month for Max 5x, $200 per month for Max 20x, and up to $500 per month pooled across users on Team plans.

Both changes were announced alongside the launch of Claude Haiku 5.5, the company’s new small model, in the “Further updates” section of the Claude Haiku 5.5 announcement. Anthropic described the moves as improvements to the value of its models and products.

## Sonnet 5.5 Cache-Read Pricing

The reduction applies to cache reads, the tokens billed when a subsequent API request retrieves previously cached content. Cache reads on Sonnet 5.5 now cost $0.10 per million tokens rather than $0.20. Because cache reads make up a large share of models’ token consumption, Anthropic said, the change reduces the cost of running Sonnet 5.5 on most agentic tasks by around 20%. The company illustrated the shift with a Terminal-Bench 4.0 chart plotting Sonnet 5.5’s accuracy against cost per attempt at both the old and new cache-read rates.

The prompt-caching section of Anthropic’s Claude Platform pricing documentation states that a cache hit now costs 5% of the standard input price on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5: $0.20 per million tokens on Opus 5.5 and $0.10 on Sonnet 5.5. The documentation lists a 2.5% rate on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 and the standard 10% rate on all other models. Under its multiplier system, five-minute cache writes are billed at 1.25 times the base input price and one-hour writes at twice the base input price. Sonnet 5.5’s remaining rates are unchanged: $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output tokens, $2.50 per million tokens for five-minute cache writes, and $4 per million tokens for one-hour cache writes.

Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 5.5 on September 28, 2026, pricing it the same as Sonnet 5 at $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output tokens, and $0.20 per million tokens for cache reads. The new rate replaces that launch cache-read price while leaving the rest of the model’s pricing intact.

## Monthly API Credits by Plan

The second change adds a recurring monthly credit for the Claude Platform, Anthropic’s API environment. Anthropic said the credit is designed to let subscribers experiment with building tools, apps, and agents that call its API, and that it can be used on any of the company’s models. Per the program’s Help Center terms, Max 5x subscribers receive $100 per month and Max 20x subscribers receive $200 per month. On Team plans, credits accrue per seat ($20 per Standard seat and $100 per Premium seat) and pool into a single monthly balance capped at $500. Discounted Team plans, including Nonprofit and Scientists plans, receive the same per-seat amounts. Anthropic’s worked example gives a team with three Standard seats and two Premium seats $260 a month, and states that adding another Premium seat would raise the next cycle’s credits to $360. The pool is calculated from the seats on the plan each time credits are deposited.

Free, Pro, and Enterprise plans are not eligible. A Max or Team subscription must be active and in good standing, and new subscribers can claim once they have been on an eligible plan for seven days. Subscriptions can be purchased on the web, iOS, or Android, but credits are claimed on claude.ai in a web browser, with no payment method required on the Claude Platform. On this page

Claude Sonnet 5.5 cache reads now cost $0.10 per million tokens, down from $0.20. The change took effect October 7, 2026, according to Anthropic's API release notes. The cache read rate is now 0.05x the $2 base input price instead of 0.1x. Input ($2), output ($10), 5-minute cache writes ($2.50) and 1-hour cache writes ($4) did not move.

What that does to your bill depends on one number: the share of your old Sonnet 5.5 spend that was cache reads. Only that line halved, so your percentage saving is half of that share. Anthropic's "around 20%" is its estimate for most agentic tasks. A cache-heavy coding agent at high effort can save closer to 30%; a short chat with a small cached prompt saves a few percent.

Three conditions change the figure you should expect:

- Where you run it. Batch, US-only inference and some cloud regions use a different cache read rate ($0.05, $0.11, $0.11). The surface table below lists each one.
- Which model. Claude Sonnet 5 still charges $0.20 for cache reads. Opus 5.5 charges $0.20, which now makes it exactly twice Sonnet 5.5 on every price line.
- How you pay. The cut is API-only. Claude Pro, Max and Team plan limits in Claude Code did not change.

## Sonnet 5.5 price table after October 7: only the cache read line moved

Anthropic's Claude API pricing page lists the cache read line as "Cache hits and refreshes", because a read also resets the cache entry's time-to-live. The multiplier table on the same page calls it "Cache read (hit)". Google Cloud labels it "Cache Hit", and Amazon Bedrock's Converse API reports it as `cacheReadInputTokens`. They are the same line, and "cached input" usually means it too.

All prices are USD per million tokens on the Claude API with default global routing, as of October 12, 2026.

| Price line | Sonnet 5.5 before Oct 7 | Sonnet 5.5 now | Sonnet 5 | Opus 5.5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base input | $2 | $2 | $2 | $4 |
| 5-minute cache write | $2.50 | $2.50 | $2.50 | $5 |
| 1-hour cache write | $4 | $4 | $4 | $8 |
| Cache read (hit and refresh) | $0.20 (0.1x) | $0.10 (0.05x) | $0.20 (0.1x) | $0.20 (0.05x) |
| Output | $10 | $10 | $10 | $20 |

Two details in that table explain most of the confusion. Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5 share every other price, so a $0.20 cache read figure for "Sonnet" is correct for Sonnet 5 and outdated for Sonnet 5.5. Opus 5.5 already used the 0.05x multiplier; its $0.20 is 5% of a $4 input price. The Claude Sonnet 5 pricing breakdown covers Sonnet 5's rates after its canceled September increase.

The release note dates the change to October 7, 2026 and says nothing about re-rating earlier usage. Expect cache reads billed before that date to stay at $0.20.
